subject: Discovery recap — BrightCart embeddings & reranking (index scale, targets, next steps)
messages:
From: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>

Cc: Rishi Malhotra <rishi_malhotra@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 14 Sep 2026 16:02:00 -0700
Subject: Discovery recap — BrightCart embeddings & reranking (index scale, targets, next steps)

Thanks again for your time today — great conversation. Quick recap from our call and the explicit success criteria / constraints you shared so we’re aligned: 

Pain points / goals
- Relevance drop for long-tail SKUs at scale (search CTR down ~18% for product pages with sparse metadata).
- Current OpenAI embedding cost is a major line item; looking to reduce embedding egress costs and get better tail latency for rerank.
- Need predictable latency for reranking at peak, and easier infra ownership for experiments.

Current stack (what you told us)
- Embeddings: OpenAI for generation today (batch & real-time)
- Vector store: Pinecone (index sharded by namespace)
- Metadata: Postgres (product attributes)
- Candidate generation: Elastic + simple keyword filters -> top N (typically 8–20) -> rerank by vector similarity
- Traffic pattern: steady QPS during daytime, big nightly ingestion (full + diffs)

Scale & batch patterns
- Current index: ~120M vectors (product descriptions + variants)
- Expected growth: 3–4x over 12 months (aiming for ~400–500M)
- Nightly bulk updates: ~5M new/updated vectors per night
- Hourly incremental batches: ~50k–200k vectors depending on campaign

Performance / cost targets
- Rerank p99 target: <= 120 ms (query side, end-to-end)
- Typical tail requirement: p95 < 60 ms, p99 < 120 ms for 8-candidate rerank
- Cost target: reduce embedding spend by at least 3x vs current OpenAI spend (we discussed open-models + local inference)
- Peak QPS target for pilot: ~2k QPS (burst to 3k)

Success criteria for a pilot
- Demonstrate p99 <= 120 ms on 8-candidate reranks at production-like queries
- Show embedding cost reduction (>= 3x) for steady-state volume in pilot window
- Integration with Pinecone metadata namespaces + low-friction ingest pipeline

Next steps we agreed
- I’ll send: architecture checklist, sample load profile, and a 3-week pilot plan (sandbox + success metrics).
- You: confirm access constraints for a sandbox (IP allowlist/VPN) and provide a representative sample of vector+metadata (anonymized) and peak QPS windows.

Attachments: call recording + SOW draft attached below.

Thanks — I’ll aim to follow up with a proposed pilot plan & times for a tech deep-dive tomorrow.

Best,
Marissa Cole

Thanks Marissa — this is perfect and matches what we discussed. A couple clarifications from our side: 

- Confirming vector store is Pinecone for embeddings and we keep product metadata in Postgres (we use a lightweight namespace scheme per locale).
- We currently batch-create embeddings via OpenAI for nightly ingest but are actively evaluating open embeddings models (or hosting embeddings ourselves) to cut costs.
- For the pilot, we’ll need either a short SLA for availability or a Dedicated option for the 3-week window — can you outline that in the pilot doc?
- On scale: the 120M number is the current live index; our backlog (including variants and test SKUs) would push to ~200–250M if included. Long term growth expectation is still 400–500M.

I’ll confirm sample data export by EOD tomorrow and can share a sanitized slice of 1M vectors + metadata for the sandbox. Also looping in Lena (product) to help scope success metrics.

Jordan
Principal Product Manager, BrightCart
